title: Runtime Authorizer Bridge: evaluation caching and adaptive middleware for RBAC v2
creator: Aisha Gupta
description: Goal: Ship a low-latency, horizontally scalable 'Authorizer Bridge' that sits as middleware in the API/runtime/console callpaths and integrates with the RBAC v2 policy evaluation engine. The bridge will provide: 1) a compact, safe decision cache (keys: principal+resource+action+context-hash) with TTL and immediate invalidation on policy updates; 2) a fast-path adaptive middleware that attempts a constant-time role/perm lookup and falls back to full AST-based evaluator for complex rules; 3) unified audit enrichment (correlation IDs, decision_reason, matched_rule_ids) that flows into existing audit pipeline; 4) admin guardrails surfaced in Console (dry-run mode, policy-change preview, impact estimation). Success criteria: p50 auth latency < 0.2ms, p95 < 1.2ms for cache hits; end-to-end API request p95 auth overhead < 1.5ms; deterministic invalidation within 2s of policy change; audit entries include request_id and policy_delta hash. Scope excludes SAML identity provider integration (separate SSO work) but includes mapping of SAML groups to RBAC roles in the Console UX. Constraints: memory per node budget of 1.5GB for decision caches, must maintain deterministic behavior for canary rollouts and allow transparent fallback to legacy RBAC v1 for flagged tenants. Out of scope: migration tooling to convert v1 policies automatically (tracked separately).
acceptance_criteria: 1) Middleware integrated in API/gateway and runtime path with feature flag; 2) Decision cache with configurable TTL and invalidation events; 3) End-to-end benchmark demonstrating target latencies and 2x throughput improvement for typical chat workloads; 4) Audit events emitted to infra audit pipeline with request_id + decision_reason for 100% of auth decisions; 5) Console exposes 'preview' and 'dry-run' for admin edits; 6) Automated tests covering policy update invalidation, cache consistency, and canary rollback behavior.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: stale allow decisions could lead to unauthorized access. Mitigation: conservative default TTL (30s), immediate invalidation on policy write events, and explicit policy-change grace period for high-risk resources. Risk: cache memory blowup for high cardinality contexts (tenant-specific scope). Mitigation: LRU with adaptive per-tenant weight and eviction metrics + circuit-breaker to bypass cache when memory pressure observed. Risk: audit volume spike. Mitigation: sampling knobs and burst buffering to audit pipeline.
implementation_notes: Architecture: Authorizer Bridge will offer a Go gRPC service embedded as middleware and a lightweight in-process library for Console. Decision cache uses sharded LRU + jemalloc tuning; invalidation via policy-change events on Kafka bus (policy-service emits topic 'policy.v2.changes'). Fast-path uses precomputed role-bitsets per principal scoped by tenant; fallback evaluator runs WASM-based policy VM to keep parity with cloud evaluator. Feature flags: 'rbac_v2.authorizer_bridge' and 'rbac_v2.cache_enabled'. Observability: tracer spans 'authz.bridge' and metrics authz_decisions_total{outcome, cache_hit} and authz_latency_ms buckets. Memory budgets and kernel tunables will be configurable in runtime-1.20 release config.
qa_and_testing_plan: Unit tests for cache correctness and invalidation; integration tests against policy-service test fixtures; synthetic load test (k6) with 200k auth checks/min to validate p95; chaos test: drop policy-change events and verify stale detection; security fuzzing on policy AST to ensure no action injection. Test artifacts: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/3421, https://ci.redwood-inference.internal/job/eng-authz-bridge/78/
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary): enable middleware + cache for internal tenants only; monitor authz_latency_ms and authz_allowed_rate for 72h. Phase 2 (gradual): add 10% tenants/week with auto-rollback on increased deny rate or latency SLO misses. Phase 3: enable Console preview and dry-run for admins, collect feedback, then flip default to enabled. Emergency rollback: toggle 'rbac_v2.authorizer_bridge' to false at gateway or disable consumer on kafka to stop invalidation events.
notes: Benchmark PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/3450 - microbench shows ~3x throughput improvement for policy-heavy workloads (cache hit ratio ~0.78)
